before_object.statement: For every commutative $R$, unit $q$ and partition $\lambda$ there is an explicit perfect $R$-bilinear star-balanced pairing $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\times P(\lambda)\to R$, giving $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\cong P(\lambda)^\circ$ naturally under all coefficient-ring base changes. Equivalently, the kernel of the row-permutation quotient onto $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is the orthogonal complement of $P(\lambda)$ for the independently defined permutation form, and its preimage in $M(\lambda)$ is $M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda}$. The pairing matrix on the actual standard bases has determinant a unit in $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$; its entries and inverse are given by finite tableau formulas. No nondegeneracy of the form restricted to $P(\lambda)$ is required. No choice principle is used.

# NEW50 ordinary DJ/Murphy bridge construction

Author: `/root/repair_cell_head_classification/native50_pairing_constructor`.
Scope: the two bridge theorem IDs assigned by the parent. This note writes no native prototype, gate, state, decision, source-attempt counter or source20 carrier. It is a construction, not an independent audit. The integral constructor's final carrier was read and its Sections 1 and 3 checked as described below. The independent Murphy cellular prerequisite remains a parent-owned prerequisite check.

Work over A=Z[q,q^{-1}]. Put μ=λ', L=ell(wλ), N=ell(w0(Sμ)), and Pν(q)=Σ_{u∈Sν}q^{ell(u)}. Use exactly the rowmodule, DJ generator, Murphy quotient, star and θ normalizations of NEW50. In particular z=xλ T_wλ yμ, θ(Ti)=q−1−Ti, and θ(xμ)=q^N yμ. All coefficient computations below are in this Laurent ring; no quantum factorial is inverted in the integral module construction.

## Exact integral input and its boundary

The independent integral constructor supplies these precise lemmas in `../integral-constructor/constructive-proof.md`, Sections 1 and 3:

* xα H yν=0 whenever α is not dominated by ν'. This is a Laurent-polynomial identity proved by minimal double cosets and a row/column collision, with the factor (1+Ti)(1−q^{-1}Ti)=0.
* For t standard of shape μ, e_t=z T_{d(t)} has rowtabloid support weakly below t' in tableau-prefix dominance, with coefficient q^{ell(d(t))} at t'. Thus the minor obtained by projecting onto the standard λ rowtabloids is triangular with diagonal Laurent units. The e_t are independent and their span is a split submodule of Mλ.

The signed cell surjection constructed next supplies the missing spanning assertion. Consequently these two input lemmas, together with the independent Murphy cellular basis, prove the full split free DJ basis; this avoids assuming a DJ spanning theorem before using the map that proves it. The formula indexes e_t by standard μ tableaux, not by rowreading d(t) for standard λ tableaux.

## Signed conjugate map, with no guessed relations

The sign-twisted cell module identifies with θ(Mμ)/θ(Kμ), where Kμ=Mμ∩I^{▷μ}, via a↦θ(a). On θ(Mμ) define

F(θ(xμ)h)=q^{-N} xλ T_wλ θ(xμ)h=z h.

This is well defined as literal left multiplication followed by multiplication by a Laurent unit. Every higher Murphy basis element of shape ν▷μ has the form T_a^* xν T_b; its θ-image is a Laurent unit times θ(T_a)^* yν θ(T_b). The annihilation lemma gives xλ H yν=0, because ν▷λ' implies λ is not dominated by ν'. Therefore xλ T_wλ θ(I^{▷μ})=0, so F kills θ(Kμ). It induces an H-linear surjection C_M(μ)^θ→Pλ with F(c0)=z. It is surjective because z generates Pλ.

Let E=span(e_t), and let π:Mλ→E be the explicit retraction obtained by inverting the unit triangular pivot matrix. The composite πF:C_M(μ)^θ→E is surjective, because F is onto Pλ and E⊂Pλ. Both modules are free of rank f^μ. Choose the finitely many preimages of the basis vectors of E: their coordinate columns form a right inverse of the square matrix of πF. Taking determinants shows that its determinant is a unit, hence πF is an isomorphism. If p∈Pλ and π(p)=0, choose u with F(u)=p; injectivity of πF gives u=0 and p=0. For any p∈Pλ the difference p−π(p) is in this kernel, so Pλ=E. This proves simultaneously that F is an isomorphism and Pλ is split free. No field rank calculation is used.

Define Φλ=F^{-1}. Then Φλ(z)=c0 and, for every h∈H,

Φλ(z h)=c0 θ(h),

where the right side is computed using the ordinary action on C_M(μ), and regarded as a vector in its θ twist. In particular Φλ(e_t)=c0 θ(T_{d(t)}). This is an actual relation-respecting map, not an assignment to the untransformed Murphy standard vector c_t. The latter assignment would generally be wrong.

For any R and unit q_R, tensor this isomorphism. Because Pλ is split in Mλ and Mλ is split free in H by the distinguished coset basis, its tensor image is exactly the actual right ideal z_R H_R. The Murphy quotient, its higher kernel and their bases commute with base change. Hence the result holds over every commutative coefficient ring, including rings with zero divisors.

## Same-shape perfect cross-pairing

Let τ:H→A take the coefficient of T_1. The standard-basis multiplication gives τ(T_u^* T_v)=δ_{u,v}q^{ell(u)}, and τ(ab)=τ(ba). These identities follow by induction from the quadratic multiplication rule. For distinguished d,e∈Dλ, length-additive row-coset multiplication gives

τ(T_d^* xλ T_e)=δ_{d,e}q^{ell(d)}.

Therefore, for a=xλ h and b=xλ g,

τ(a^*b)=Pλ(q) β(a,b).

This equality is first a polynomial identity on distinguished basis vectors and then follows by bilinearity.

If a∈Kλ=Mλ∩I^{▷λ} and p∈Pλ, then a^*p=0. Indeed every higher Murphy element of shape ν▷λ is T_r^* xν T_s, and each product with p=xλ T_wλ yλ' h vanishes by xν H yλ'=0, since ν is not dominated by λ. Thus Pλ(q) β(a,p)=0. The Laurent ring is a domain and Pλ(q) is a nonzero Laurent polynomial, so β(a,p)=0. No cancellation is performed in a specialized ring: the identity is established universally and then specialized with the supplied base-change-compatible kernel basis.

The formula

Bλ(a+Kλ,p)=β(a,p)

is consequently well defined and star-balanced. It gives a homomorphism C_M(λ)→Pλ^circ. The diagonal matrix of β on the rowmodule has unit entries q^{ell(d)}, so Mλ→Mλ^* is an isomorphism. Since Pλ is a split submodule, restriction Mλ^*→Pλ^* is surjective. Hence Mλ→Pλ^* is surjective, and because Kλ is killed it factors as a surjection C_M(λ)→Pλ^circ. Both are free of rank f^λ. Its determinant is a unit, hence it is an isomorphism. Its kernel in Mλ is exactly Kλ=Pλ^⊥. After every base change the same inverse matrix proves perfectness and the same kernel identity.

This is a genuine perfect cross-pairing and requires no nondegeneracy of the restricted DJ form. Explicit entries on the actual bases are finite formulas: expand e_t in the distinguished rowbasis as e_t=Σ_d a_{td} xλT_d; for a standard λ tableau s,

Bλ(c_s,e_t)=q^{ell(d(s))}a_{t,d(s)}.

The coefficients a_{td} are obtained by expanding the finite signed symmetrizer and the word T_wλ T_u T_{d(t)} with the quadratic multiplication rules. The inverse pairing matrix is det(B)^{-1}adj(B); det(B) is a Laurent unit by the preceding proof. This is a finite tableau formula, not an unspecified inverse in a generic field.

## Universal form identity and the exact unit

The initial DJ generator expands as

z=Σ_{u∈Sμ}(-q)^{-ell(u)} xλ T_{wλu}.

Each wλu is distinguished for the λ rowmodule, these cosets are distinct, and ell(wλu)=L+ell(u). To see rowstandardness, each λ row picks one entry from each consecutive interval corresponding to a column of λ; permuting within the separate intervals preserves its increasing order. Minimality and length additivity are the standard minimal-double-coset property. Thus

β(z,z)=q^L Σ_{u∈Sμ}q^{-ell(u)}=q^{L-N}Pμ(q).

The last equality pairs u with w0(Sμ)u. On the independent Murphy cell, xμ^2=Pμ(q)xμ gives Gμ(c0,c0)=Pμ(q). Therefore the only possible proportionality factor with Φ(z)=c0 is

uλ(q)=q^{N-L}.

Here is a choice-free local justification that the comparison of generator norms determines the whole form, without using generic rank to establish an integral lattice claim. Over K=Q(q), the regular trace bilinear form (a,b)↦Tr_K(L_ab) has determinant a polynomial nonzero at q=1: there H is Q[S_n], where its standard-basis matrix is n! times the permutation matrix pairing u with u^{-1}. Thus this form is nondegenerate over K. The Jacobson radical of a finite-dimensional algebra is nilpotent; for a in that radical and any b, L_ab is nilpotent and has trace zero. Nondegeneracy forces the radical to vanish, so H_K is semisimple.

In a semisimple cellular algebra every cell form is nondegenerate and the cell module has full matrix algebra acting on it. One can verify this directly, without a splitting-field or absolute-choice assumption: linearly extend the finite cell order and take the corresponding successive semisimple quotient ideals. A cell layer is C⊗C with multiplication (a⊗b)(c⊗d)=G(b,c)a⊗d. If G were degenerate, (rad G)⊗C would be a nonzero square-zero ideal stable under the surrounding algebra by contravariance and the cell law. This contradicts semisimplicity of the quotient. Invertibility of G then realizes every rank-one operator, so every module endomorphism of C is scalar. This also proves that any two nonzero contravariant forms on C are proportional: use one nonsingular Gram matrix to turn the other into a commuting endomorphism.

After the integral isomorphism F has been established, transfer β to C_M(μ)^θ. The Murphy form Gμ is nondegenerate generically, and the transferred form is nonzero because its initial value q^{L-N}Pμ(q) is nonzero. The preceding endomorphism calculation makes the forms proportional over K. Comparing their initial values gives, for all integral x,y∈Pλ,

Gμ^θ(Φλx,Φλy)=q^{N-L}β(x,y).

Both sides have entries in A. Their equality over its fraction field implies equality in A, so tensoring proves the identity over every commutative R with unit parameter. This method neither divides by Pμ after specialization nor discards a lattice index. It uses generic semisimplicity only for uniqueness of an already integral pair of forms.

## Consequences, including all fields at q=1

The form identity multiplies by a unit, so after every coefficient specialization Φ sends the DJ form radical exactly onto the radical of the twisted conjugate Murphy form. The quotient isomorphism includes the zero-quotient case. Over a PID, for a chosen prime π and every i≥0, x lies in the ith divisibility submodule precisely when β(x,P)⊂π^i; the unit-scaled identity and the isomorphism Φ make this equivalent to the corresponding Murphy condition. Thus all these submodules and reductions correspond.

The perfect pairing gives C_M(λ)≅Pλ^circ; the signed conjugate map for λ' gives Pλ'≅C_M(λ)^θ. Combining them yields Pλ'≅Pλ^{circ,θ}. The conjugate cell itself satisfies C_M(λ')≅Pλ^θ, without an additional dual.

At q=1, all exponents give unit 1, θ is the sign automorphism, and the permutation form is the usual tabloid form. Consequently the module and form comparisons hold over every field, including characteristic two and cases where the form radical is the whole module. Empty shapes use L=N=0 and the scalar 1.

The final integral carrier was read. Its collision factorization in Section 1 and its prefix-count induction in Section 3 check correctly. For completeness, the standard ascending chain used there exists as follows: view standard tableaux as linear extensions of the Young-node partial order. Bubble-sort the desired extension toward rowreading order by adjacent inversions. Any swapped pair is incomparable, because comparable nodes have the same order in both linear extensions. Each swap removes one inversion relative to rowreading; reversing the sorting supplies an ascending standard chain from t^μ, with the exact additive-length permutations required in Section 3. In particular every transpose swap has i in the lower row and i+1 in the upper row, so the q coefficient and the two prefix-count bounds used in that proof apply.

## Statement

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $q\in R^\times$ and $\lambda\vdash n$, and let $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with its basis $\{m_t\}$, $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$, the permutation form $\beta$ on $M(\lambda)$ and the DJ form on $P(\lambda)$ be as in [[def-dj-bridge-row-column-permutation-modules-and-polytabloids]], [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening]]. Then:

1. Setting $B_\lambda(m_s,p):=\beta(x_\lambda T_{d_\lambda(s)},p)$ for $s\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)$ and $p\in P(\lambda)$ defines an explicit $R$-bilinear pairing $B_\lambda\colon C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\times P(\lambda)\to R$ that is $H$-balanced, $B_\lambda(mh,p)=B_\lambda(m,ph^*)$, and whose adjoint $c\mapsto B_\lambda(c,-)$ is an isomorphism of right $H$-modules $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\to P(\lambda)^\circ$ onto the star-contragredient module of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. No nondegeneracy of the DJ form $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ is required.

2. Equivalently, the kernel of the quotient map $M(\lambda)\to C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ is the orthogonal complement $P(\lambda)^\perp=\{a\in M(\lambda):\beta(a,p)=0\text{ for all }p\in P(\lambda)\}$, namely $M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda}$; the pairing matrices in the bases $\{m_s\}$ and $\{e_t\}$ have entries $B_\lambda(m_s,e_t)=q^{\ell(d_\lambda(s))}a_{d_\lambda(s),t}$ with $e_t=\sum_d a_{d,t}b_d$, and determinant a unit of $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$. Their inverses are finite tableau formulas given by the adjugate divided by this unit.

3. All statements are compatible with every base change $A\to R$, $v\mapsto q$; the construction uses no generic semisimplicity, no nondegeneracy of $\beta_{P(\lambda)}$ and no choice principle.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A commutative ring $R$, $q\in R^\times$, a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, the Hecke algebra $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ with its standard basis, star anti-involution, the modules $M(\lambda)=x_\lambda H\supseteq P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$, the distinguished basis $\{b_r=x_\lambda T_{d_\lambda(r)}\}$ of $M(\lambda)$ and the permutation form $\beta$, the Murphy basis $\{m^\rho_{st}\}$, the dominance ideal $I^{\rhd\lambda}$, the cell module $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ with basis $\{m_s\}$ and the Murphy form $G_\lambda$.

[F1] The trace $\tau\colon H\to R$, $\tau(T_w)=\delta_{w,1}$, satisfies $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$ and $\tau(a^*b)=B_0(a,b)=\delta_{u,v}q^{\ell(u)}$ for standard basis elements $a=T_u$, $b=T_v$; the bilinear form $\tau(a^*b)$ has unit diagonal in the standard basis ([[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]]).

[F2] $M(\lambda)$ is free on $\{b_r\}$, $\beta(b_r,b_v)=\delta_{r,v}q^{\ell(d_\lambda(r))}$, and $\beta$ is $H$-contravariant; $P(\lambda)$ is free on $\{e_t=z_\lambda T_{d_\lambda'(t)}\}$ and a split direct summand of $M(\lambda)$ ([[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]], [[lem-dj-bridge-permutation-form-invariance-and-restriction]], [[lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening]]).

[F3] $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)=M(\lambda)/(M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda})$, $K:=M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda}$ is the kernel of the quotient, $I^{\rhd\lambda}$ is spanned by the Murphy elements $m^\nu_{uv}$ with $\nu\rhd\lambda$, and $\{m_s\}$ is an $R$-basis of the cell module ([[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]]).

[F4] $x_\kappa Hy_\rho=0$ whenever $\sum_{i\le k}\kappa_i>\sum_{i\le k}\rho'_i$ for some $k\ge1$ ([[lem-dj-bridge-parabolic-double-coset-annihilation]]).

[F5] The star-contragredient $N^\circ=\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R)$ of a right $H$-module is a right $H$-module via $(fh)(m)=f(mh^*)$; for finite free $N$ it is finite free of the same rank and $(-)^\circ$ commutes with base change ([[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]).





## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The correctly scaled universal trace formula.** Work first over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$, using $q=v$ as the formal parameter. For $d,e\in D_\lambda$, length additivity gives $b_d=\sum_{u\in S_\lambda}T_{ud}$, and [F1] gives $\tau(b_d^*b_e)=0$ when $d\ne e$, while $\tau(b_d^*b_d)=\sum_{u\in S_\lambda}q^{\ell(ud)}=q^{\ell(d)}P_\lambda(q)$, where $P_\lambda(q):=\sum_{u\in S_\lambda}q^{\ell(u)}$. By bilinearity, $$\tau(a^*b)=P_\lambda(q)\,\beta(a,b)\qquad(a,b\in M_A(\lambda)).$$ The factor $P_\lambda$ is essential; it is not generally a unit and can vanish after specialization. It is nonzero in the domain $A$, since its constant coefficient is $1$. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 **Orthogonality before specialization.** Put $K_A=M_A(\lambda)\cap I_A^{\rhd\lambda}$ and $p=z_\lambda h$. For a higher Murphy element $m^\nu_{uv}=T_{d_\nu(u)}^*x_\nu T_{d_\nu(v)}$ with $\nu\rhd\lambda$, its product with $p$ after star is $$ (m^\nu_{uv})^*p=T_{d_\nu(v)}^*x_\nu\bigl(T_{d_\nu(u)}x_\lambda T_{w_\lambda}\bigr)y_{\lambda'}h=0,$$ because $x_\nu Hy_{\lambda'}=0$ by [F4]. The outer factor multiplies a zero vector; no factor is silently discarded. Expand $k\in K_A$ in the higher Murphy basis using [F3]. Then $k^*p=0$ and step 1.1 gives $P_\lambda(q)\beta(k,p)=0$. Cancel this nonzero polynomial only in the universal domain $A$, proving $\beta(K_A,P_A)=0$. The quotient and its kernel in [F3] are base-change compatible: the quotient is free on the supplied standard basis, its kernel is the split kernel of that quotient, and the independent Murphy construction identifies its specialization with $M_R(\lambda)\cap I_R^{\rhd\lambda}$. Thus tensoring the zero pairing identity gives $\beta(K_R,P_R)=0$ for every $R$ and unit $q$. No cancellation is performed in $R$, including when $P_\lambda(q)=0$. [step 1.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 **The descended pairing is perfect.** Define $B_\lambda(a+K_R,p)=\beta(a,p)$; step 2.1 proves this is well defined. Contravariance gives $B_\lambda(ch,p)=B_\lambda(c,ph^*)$, so its adjoint $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\to P(\lambda)^\circ$ is an $H$-homomorphism by [F5]. The map $M(\lambda)\to M(\lambda)^\circ$, $a\mapsto\beta(a,-)$, is an isomorphism with unit diagonal $q^{\ell(d)}$. Compose this map itself with restriction $M(\lambda)^\circ\to P(\lambda)^\circ$, which is onto because $P(\lambda)$ is split in $M(\lambda)$. The resulting surjection kills $K_R$ and therefore factors onto $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\to P(\lambda)^\circ$. Both are free of rank $f^\lambda$. Choosing preimages of their finitely many basis vectors gives a right inverse of its square matrix; the determinant is a unit, so the adjoint is an isomorphism. This proves clause 1 without any nondegeneracy of the DJ self-form. [step 2.1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

4.1 **Kernel, finite formulas and every base change.** The kernel of $M(\lambda)\to P(\lambda)^\circ$ is $P(\lambda)^\perp$ by its definition. Since the factored adjoint is an isomorphism, this is exactly $K_R=M(\lambda)\cap I^{\rhd\lambda}$. Write $e_t=\sum_d a_{d,t}b_d$ with the finite Laurent-polynomial coefficients of the integral polytabloid basis. Then $B_\lambda(m_s,e_t)=q^{\ell(d_\lambda(s))}a_{d_\lambda(s),t}$. Compute these coefficients by the finite signed-symmetrizer expansion and standard-basis multiplication; the inverse pairing matrix is $\det(B_\lambda)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(B_\lambda)$. Over $A$ its determinant is a Laurent unit by step 3.1, so both the pairing and its inverse specialize to every $R$, retaining perfectness and the kernel identity. Empty shapes have the rank-one pairing $1$. No generic semisimplicity, nondegeneracy of the DJ self-form, division by a specialized Poincaré polynomial or choice principle is used. before_object.statement:
For every commutative $R$, unit $q$ and partition $\lambda$, there is a base-change compatible isomorphism
$$\Phi_\lambda:P(\lambda)\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$$
of right $H$-modules, and an explicit unit $u_\lambda(q)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}\in A^\times$ such that
$$G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\,\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)\qquad(x,y\in P(\lambda)),$$
with $G_{\lambda'}$ the Murphy form of [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and $\theta$ the sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. The unit $u_\lambda$ is computed in the fixed generator and form normalizations of this page; no unnamed scalar and no potentially vanishing scalar is permitted. Consequently the form radicals and their quotients correspond after every field specialization: $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including the zero-quotient case. Over a PID with a chosen prime, the unit-scaled form identity preserves all Jantzen divisibility submodules and reductions. One also obtains $P(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with the exact position of the dual and $\theta$, separating same-shape duality from conjugate-sign transport. ## Statement

Assume the isomorphism $\Phi_\lambda$ and the exact unit identity of [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Then:

1. For every commutative ring $R$ and $q=1$, the module $P(\lambda)$ identifies with the ordinary integral-polytabloid Specht module $R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}S^\lambda_{\mathbb Z}$ of [[def-integral-specht-lattice-and-base-change]], with the classical left action converted to a right action by $x\cdot w=w^{-1}x$: the basis $\{e_t=z_\lambda T_{d_{\lambda'}(t)}\}$ specializes to the standard polytabloid basis and the DJ form to the standard tabloid form. The sign automorphism $\theta$ becomes the pullback along the sign twist $w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$ of $R[S_n]$. Over every field $F$, this specialization is compatible with the conjugate-sign dictionary of [[lem-conjugate-specht-sign-duality-over-fields]].

2. For a field $F$, a unit $q\in F^\times$ and partitions $\mu,\lambda\vdash n$ with $D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}\ne0$ one has $[P(\lambda):D^{\mu}_{\mathrm{DJ}}]=[C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda'):D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}]$, and the simultaneous sign-automorphism pullback is the same $\theta$ on both sides: $(D^{\mu}_{\mathrm{DJ}})^\theta\cong D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}$.

3. Suppose a Schur-algebra corner is already proved to send the Weyl module $W(\lambda)$ to $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ and its head $L(\lambda)$ to $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$. Then that corner gives $F(W(\lambda'))\cong P(\lambda)^\theta$ and $F(L(\lambda'))\cong(D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}})^\theta$, including the zero case; this is the $\theta$-twisted conjugate dictionary, never the untwisted conjugate-dual identity. No Schur-algebra theorem and no source-20 convention is a prerequisite of this conditional dictionary.

No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A field $F$ or a commutative ring $R$ with a unit $q$, a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, the module $P(\lambda)=z_\lambda H$ with its basis $\{e_t\}$, its DJ form and its form quotient $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$, the cell module $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ with basis $\{m_t\}$ and form quotient $D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M}$, the sign automorphism $\theta$, and the isomorphism and unit identity of [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]].

[F1] $\Phi_\lambda\colon P(\lambda)\to C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$ is an $H$-module isomorphism with $G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)$ and $u_\lambda(q)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}$ ([[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]).

[F2] $\theta$ is the involutive sign automorphism; the twist $M^\theta$ has action $m\cdot h=m\theta(h)$, is exact, preserves composition multiplicities and maps simple modules to simple modules; at $q=1$ over a field, $\theta$ is the pullback along $w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$ ([[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]).

[F3] $S^\lambda_{\mathbb Z}$ has the standard polytabloids as a $\mathbb Z$-basis and is base-change compatible: for every commutative ring $R$ the canonical map $R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}S^\lambda_{\mathbb Z}\to R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M^\lambda_{\mathbb Z}$ is injective onto the span of the polytabloids in the tabloid module, and the standard polytabloids form an $R$-basis of the image ([[def-integral-specht-lattice-and-base-change]]).

[F4] The conjugate-sign dictionary $S^\lambda_F\otimes\operatorname{sgn}\cong(S^{\lambda'}_F)^*$ holds over every field, with the explicit sign-twisted tabloid homomorphism ([[lem-conjugate-specht-sign-duality-over-fields]]).

[F5] The Hecke algebra has presentation $(T_i-q)(T_i+1)=0$, braid and distant commutation, with standard basis $(T_w)_w$; $S_n$ has the Coxeter presentation $s_i^2=1$ with the same braid and distant commutation relations ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], [[thm-the-symmetric-group-has-the-coxeter-presentation]]). The row-module and polytabloid bases are split and compatible with every coefficient-ring base change ([[lem-dj-bridge-row-permutation-module-standard-action]], [[lem-dj-bridge-integral-murphy-and-polytabloid-straightening]]).

[F6] The Murphy cell law and the cell form are defined by formulas with coefficients in $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1}]$ and commute with base change; the independent same-shape perfect pairing gives $C_{\mathrm M}(\rho)\cong P(\rho)^\circ$ ([[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]], [[thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual]]).





## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The group algebra over every coefficient ring.** Let $R$ be any commutative ring and specialize at $q=1$. The Hecke relations become $T_i^2=1$, braid and distant commutation. The Coxeter presentation in [F5] therefore gives the homomorphism $H_{R,1}(S_n)\to R[S_n]$ carrying $T_i$ to $s_i$. A reduced word shows that it carries every $T_w$ to $w$. These are bases of the source and target over $R$, so the map is an isomorphism over $R$, including in positive characteristic and with zero divisors. Equivalently the assignment $s_i\mapsto T_i$ gives its inverse directly from the presentation. No complex-field specialization, dimension comparison over a field or semisimplicity is used. [F5, algebra]

1.2 **Multiplicities and zero quotients.** For a field and unit $q$, the unit form identity in [F1] identifies $D^{\mu}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ with $(D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including zero quotients. A nonzero cell-form quotient is simple: the cell rank-one action shows that every vector outside its radical generates the cell module, so the radical is its unique maximal submodule. Thus when $D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}\ne0$, the module $D^{\mu}_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ is a legitimate simple composition-factor label. Applying the exact twist equivalence in [F2] to a composition series and using [F1] gives $$[P(\lambda):D^{\mu}_{\mathrm{DJ}}]=[C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta:D^{\mu}_{\mathrm{DJ}}]=[C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda'):(D^{\mu}_{\mathrm{DJ}})^\theta]=[C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda'):D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}].$$ This proves clause 2. If a form is identically zero, only its zero form quotient is asserted; no claim is made that the actual module head vanishes. [F1, F2, F6, algebra]

2.1 **The actual polytabloids and the forms.** Give the classical tabloid module the right action $\{t\}\cdot w=\{w^{-1}\cdot t\}=\{t\cdot w\}$. The map $b_d=x_\lambda T_d\mapsto\{t^\lambda\cdot d\}$ sends the distinguished basis to the tabloid basis. It respects the right action: at $q=1$ the row-module multiplication rule is simply the permutation of these cosets, with a same-row transposition acting as $1$. Every diagonal value of $\beta$ becomes $1$, so this is an isometry to the orthonormal tabloid form. The column group of the column-filled tableau $t_\lambda$ is exactly $S_{\lambda'}$, because its columns carry the consecutive row blocks of $\lambda'$. Hence $z_\lambda=x_\lambda w_\lambda\sum_{u\in S_{\lambda'}}\operatorname{sgn}(u)u$ maps to $\sum_u\operatorname{sgn}(u)\{t_\lambda\cdot u\}$, the classical column polytabloid of $t_\lambda$ (replace $u$ by $u^{-1}$ to compare with the left-action formula). Covariance shows $e_t=z_\lambda d_{\lambda'}(t)$ maps to the polytabloid of $t_\lambda\cdot d_{\lambda'}(t)=t'$, the transpose of the standard $\lambda'$-tableau $t$. Thus the actual standard bases correspond bijectively. By the split integral classical basis in [F3] and the split Hecke basis in [F5], this identifies $P(\lambda)$ with $R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}S^\lambda_{\mathbb Z}$ over every $R$, and the restricted DJ form with the restricted tabloid form. [F3, F5, F6, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **The exact position of the twist.** At $q=1$, [F2] gives $\theta(T_i)=-T_i$, hence $\theta(w)=\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$. Therefore the right module $P(\lambda)^\theta$ is the sign tensor twist. Applying the involution $\theta$ to [F1] yields $$P(\lambda)^\theta\cong C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda'),$$ without a remaining twist on the Murphy cell. Combining this with the independent same-shape pairing in [F6] gives $P(\lambda)^\theta\cong P(\lambda')^\circ$. Under step 2.1, star dual is the ordinary group contragredient dual, so this is exactly the module identity $S_F^\lambda\otimes\operatorname{sgn}\cong(S_F^{\lambda'})^*$ of [F4] after converting the published left modules to right modules. This asserts the same compatible module dictionary, not an unproved equality of separately normalized explicit maps. In characteristic $2$ the sign becomes trivial at $q=1$; conjugation remains part of the identity. [F1, F2, F4, F6, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Conditional Schur dictionary and conclusion.** Under the stated separate hypothesis on a Schur corner, its images at $\lambda'$ are $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')$ and $D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M}$. The untwisted Murphy identities from step 3.1 and [F1], valid for arbitrary unit $q$ by involutivity of $\theta$, identify these with $P(\lambda)^\theta$ and $(D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}})^\theta$, including the zero quotient. This proves clause 3 without a Schur theorem as a prerequisite. The actual nonzero Schur head and the Hecke cell-form quotient are distinct notions when the corner kills the former. For the empty shape, the generators, forms, twists and all isomorphisms have value $1$. All bases, maps and scalar identities are explicit and use no choice principle. [F1, F2, F6, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎
